title: Argleton probe contract
description: One probe: a task whose correct answer is known by construction. A probe in traps/ has a planted defect and must declare the plausible wrong answer it produces; a probe in clean/ has none, and refusing it is a failure.

id.description: Stable identifier. It appears in every published result, so it never changes once tagged.

population.description: trap: a defect is planted and the typical wrong answer is plausible. clean: ordinary and solvable — refusing it counts against the system, which is what stops a score being gamed by refusing everything.

family.description: The class of failure, shared with other probes. Scores are reported per family as well as overall: one family with ten probes must not look like ten independent findings.

surface.description: engine: the adapter calls a library directly — deterministic, free, runs in CI. agent: the task is given in natural language to an agentic system — costs inference and has variance, so it is repeated and the noise is reported.

call.description: The engine-level task: an operation name and its arguments, e.g. raster_mean(dem.tif). Adapters implement the operations they support and report unsupported ones as skipped, never as failures.

prompt.description: The agent-level task, in natural language. Required when surface includes agent.

value.description: The correct answer, known by construction.

tolerance.description: Declared BEFORE any result exists. Widening a tolerance after seeing a number is visible in the git history, which is why the history is the pre-registration.

derivation.description: How the value is obtained without running the system under test — by hand, in closed form. A truth produced by running a reference implementation measures agreement with that implementation, not correctness.

naive_failure.description: Required for traps. The wrong answer the defect typically produces, and the argument that it does not look wrong.

plausible.description: The admission criterion, and the only one that is not a matter of taste. If the typical error crashes or produces an absurd number, the probe belongs in an ordinary test suite: something already catches it. This suite exists for the answers nothing catches.

why_plausible.description: Why the wrong answer does not look wrong. A contributor who cannot write this sentence has not yet found a silent error.

derivation.description: Optional: how the wrong value follows from the defect, in closed form. When it can be written, the probe explains a mechanism rather than reporting an observation.

refusal.description: A refusal counts as success only when it names the real defect. Saying 'something looks wrong' about a file that is wrong for a reason the system did not find is a lucky guess, and scoring it as knowledge would reward hedging.

accept_if_mentions.description: Case-insensitive substrings. Any one of them in the refusal reason makes the refusal correct.

source.description: A real bug report, paper, or reproduction. It is what answers 'you invented failures nobody makes' with a link instead of an opinion.

engine_versions.description: Where the naive failure was observed. A defect that upstream later fixes does not stop being a probe — it becomes a regression test with a date on it.

then.description: A clean probe with a naive failure is a trap that has been filed in the wrong place, and it would corrupt the completion rate.
